story.title: iCloud+ Hide My Email addresses will remain on icloud.com

draft:
Apple just confirmed Hide My Email will stay on iCloud.com.

The service now lives exclusively in the web UI, not in iOS Settings. For users who already manage aliases on a desktop, this is familiar ground, but it adds a click‑through for anyone trying to create an alias on the fly from their iPhone.

From a developer’s perspective, the separation means we can’t rely on a native prompt to generate an alias during sign‑up. We’ll need to guide users to the web portal or build our own flow that asks for a temporary address and then swaps it out later. It also keeps the alias data out of the device’s local storage, which could be a subtle privacy win.

I’m curious: how will this web‑only approach affect adoption of alias‑based sign‑ups in mobile‑first apps?
